nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What limitation do current LCA standards, EN 15804(2012) + A2(2019), have regarding emissions?
nodes.answer: They do not take into account the timing of when emissions occur.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What types of products have most LCA literature reviews focused on?
nodes.answer: Most LCA literature reviews have focused on consumer electronics.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are some direct life cycle impacts of electronic healthcare devices mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The direct life cycle impacts include those related to production and end-of-life of the devices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_003
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are some keywords associated with the concepts discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Keywords include LCA (Life Cycle Assessment), environmental sustainability, electronic healthcare devices, electronic surgical devices, electronic non-surgical devices, and healthcare pathway.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Are there specific areas of healthcare that have been reviewed in relation to LCA?
nodes.answer: Yes, specific areas of healthcare that have been reviewed include environmental sustainability of mobile health technologies, comparison of single-use and reusable healthcare devices, pharma-LCAs, and environmental sustainability of surgical procedures.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_005
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What gap in the literature regarding LCA studies is mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The paragraph mentions that there is no review focused on electronic health devices (EHDs) and that LCA studies of electronic surgical devices are rarely addressed.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_006
nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.question: What methodology was used to identify relevant studies in the research?
nodes.answer: The methodology involved the categorization of studies into electronic surgical and non-surgical devices and analyzing the attributes and methodological choices based on the four phases of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were the four phases of the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) that the articles were analyzed based on?
nodes.answer: The four phases of the LCA are: (i) goal and scope definition, (ii) life cycle inventory, (iii) life cycle impact assessment (LCIA), and (iv) interpretation of the impact assessment results.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What challenges were identified during the analysis of the articles in the context of LCA?
nodes.answer: Methodological challenges were identified for each LCA phase, and recommendations for these challenges were formulated.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do rented garments compare to owned garments in terms of greenhouse gas emissions according to the LCA?
nodes.answer: According to the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), rented garments have a greater life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) per piece when dry-cleaned compared to owned garments. However, the GHG emissions per wear are significantly reduced for rented garments that increase lifetime wear, such as dresses.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_010
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is one of the major uncertainties that may impact the quality of findings in the LCA methodology?
nodes.answer: One major uncertainty that may impact the quality of findings in the LCA methodology is consumer behaviours, including variables like the number of wears, laundry frequency, garment lifespans, and transportation modes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_011
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the outcome of Ncube et al. (2022) using LCA in the production of Italian extra virgin olive oil?
nodes.answer: Ncube et al. (2022) were able to carry out comparative assessments between linear and circular production, leading to the definition of proper circular strategies to reduce environmental footprints.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_012
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is a major consequence of using estimates or excluding steps in the production process within the LCA methodology?
nodes.answer: The major consequence is the compromise of assessment accuracy, which can increase variability and uncertainty in the results of the analysis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_013
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What phase of the LCA methodology is particularly affected by the lack of reliable data?
nodes.answer: The Life Cycle Inventory phase is particularly affected by the lack of reliable and accurate data.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_014
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the significance of the LCA Food Database maintained by the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment?
nodes.answer: The LCA Food Database is significant as it provides information on the environmental impact of different food products, helping consumers make more sustainable food choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_015
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do the diverse findings of LCA studies contribute to the variability in estimates of global GHG emissions associated with meat production?
nodes.answer: The diverse findings of LCA studies across different stages of production contribute to the variability in estimates of global GHG emissions associated with meat production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_016
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What novel approach has advanced the Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) method in LCA?
nodes.answer: The development of high-resolution data allows for the calculation of GHG emissions of individual finishing cattle, which represents a novel approach in Life Cycle Inventory analysis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy-efficient appliances|Life-cycle analysis of appliances_qna_017
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What must LCA studies acknowledge to ensure scientific robustness according to the consensus mentioned?
nodes.answer: LCA studies must acknowledge uncertainties inherent within production systems.
